This message comes from Brex. If your best finance people are doing expense reports and chasing
receipts, it's time to get Brex AF, agentic finance that eliminates that work before it starts.
Learn more at brex.com/af. This is NPR News Now. The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston. With just over a week until election
day, polls suggest Republicans are losing ground as they fight to keep control of Congress. The
final stretch of the campaign is giving both parties little time to persuade undecided voters
and get supporters to the polls. NPR's Mara Laison reports. Polls show President Trump's
overall approval rating at its lowest ever, and his approval rating on the economy in some polls
is under 30 percent. But the polls in the battleground House and Senate races are still
very close. In the dozen or so competitive House races, the generic ballot question,
that is, would you rather have a Democrat or Republican represent you in Congress,
Democrats are ahead by only two or three points. And the races that will decide control of the
Senate are all too close to call. In states like Alaska, Iowa, Ohio, and Texas, polls show neither
candidate ahead outside the margin of error. Democrats need to flip net four seats to take
the Senate majority. Donald Trump won all those states in 2024 by double digits. Mara Laison,
NPR News. The Democrat challenging Alaska Senator Dan Sullivan is among those asking
a federal judge to dismiss a Justice Department lawsuit. Alaska public media's Liz Ruskin reports
the suit seeks to block certification of the election if the Republican incumbent loses.
President Trump says he personally ordered the lawsuit. It would block Alaska from certifying
a win by Democrat Mary Peltola, pending an investigation to determine if voters were
confused by a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot, a retired teacher. The ballot lists one Sullivan as
the Republican incumbent, the other as Daniel J. Jr. with no party affiliation. The senators'
campaign says Alaskans can tell the difference. Still, the campaign said it would let the lawsuit
run its course. Peltola calls the lawsuit corrupt. As her attorneys put it, Trump insists Alaskans
re-elect the senator or he won't let them elect anyone at all. For NPR News, I'm Liz Ruskin in
Anchorage. The Federal Reserve will meet this week to decide whether to once again raise interest
rates. NPR's Stephen Besaha reports this will be the last time the Fed will consider moving
rates before the midterm elections. President Trump selected Kevin Worsch to chair the Federal Reserve
earlier this year, with Trump clear that he wants interest rates to go down. Instead, the Fed raised
rates in September for the first time in more than three years to tamp down inflation. Since then,
inflation has remained hotter than expected. The Labor Department reported consumer prices were up
3.7 percent in September from a year earlier. Investors still mostly expect the Fed will hold
rates steady this month, but economists also see a December rate hike as more than likely.
Stephen Besaha, NPR News. This is NPR News.
Airbnb is cracking down on checkout chores under a new policy for reservations books starting
on November 20. Hosts, for the most part, will not be allowed to require guests to strip beds,
wash dishes or take trash off the property. They can still, as guests, to gather used towels,
leave dishes in the sink and sort their recycling. Airbnb says visitors should not be doing the work
that a cleaner would normally handle. The Milwaukee Brewers have taken a two games to none lead over
the Tampa Bay Rays and Major League Baseball's World Series with a victory last night in Milwaukee.
Chuck Kornbach reports the next games will be played in Florida.
When the Brewers got the final out of their five to four comeback win over the Rays, the sellout
crowd of more than 43,000 at American Family Field erupted in cheers. Just before stepping
on the down escalator out of the ballpark, Shelly Marquart said she'll be at the next games too.
It was amazing. We're off to Tampa. We have the three games that we're going to down there.
We cannot wait. The third game of the Best of Seven World Series is scheduled for Monday
night at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg. For NPR News, I'm Chuck Kornbach in Milwaukee.
Halloween candy sales are off to a slow start as high prices continue to squeeze household
budgets. Research firm Nielsen IQ says sales fell 6.7 percent this month compared with the
year earlier. Shoppers are buying smaller bags while the candy industry says it's still hopeful
sales will pick up closer to Halloween. This is NPR. This message comes from Angie. When it comes
